last_sync.summary: Anti-lag now requires a valid driver throttle-intent signal before it can arm, and the anti-lag ETB target addition is applied only when anti-lag is enabled and the accelerator-pedal reading is valid. The ETB pedal-target page is updated to describe these conditions.

decisions.rationale: Anti-lag arming now fails closed: if the driver throttle-intent signal is missing or non-finite, the anti-lag throttle condition is false and anti-lag does not activate, even if RPM, coolant, and switch conditions are met. The anti-lag ETB target addition is also gated on anti-lag being enabled and on a valid, finite accelerator-pedal reading, so a stale active flag or a failed pedal sensor no longer adds ALSEtbAdd to the throttle target. No tune migration is required; existing anti-lag tunes keep their settings. Check that the pedal and throttle-intent sensors are calibrated and healthy before relying on anti-lag, and treat a lost pedal signal as an anti-lag inhibit rather than a fault to tune around.
evidence: firmware/controllers/algo/antilag_system.cpp: isALSMaxThrottleIntentCondition now returns false when Sensor::get(SensorType::DriverThrottleIntent) is invalid or non-finite
firmware/controllers/actuators/electronic_throttle.cpp: getSetpointEtbNonTorqueModel adds ALSEtbAdd only if antiLagEnabled and isAntilagCondition and the AcceleratorPedal reading is valid and finite
unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_antilag.cpp: new AntiLagRequiresValidThrottleIntent test covers invalid, NaN, recovery, and re-arm
unit_tests/tests/actuators/test_etb.cpp: new antiLagAdderRequiresEnabledAndValidPedal test covers stale flag, invalid pedal, and disabled anti-lag
